sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani and many others live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的现场对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在NYTimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费阅读权限，畅享我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, moments before he opened fire, the gunman asked who was on the baseball field.
sentences.zh: 今天，枪手在开火前片刻询问了棒球场上的人是谁。

sentences.en: Democrats or Republicans.
sentences.zh: 是民主党人还是共和党人。

sentences.en: An act of political violence at a moment of extreme partisanship.
sentences.zh: 在党派纷争极其激烈的时刻发生的一起政治暴力事件。

sentences.en: And what happens when a 400-year-old story about one of history's most infamous acts of political violence is adapted for today.
sentences.zh: 当一个关于历史上最臭名昭著的政治暴力行为之一的400年前的故事被改编到今天时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: It's Thursday, June 15th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月15日，星期四。

sentences.en: Michael Shearer, walk us through the scene on Wednesday morning.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·希尔，请带我们回顾一下周三早上的现场情况。

sentences.en: It was a hot morning, a humid, typical Washington summer morning.
sentences.zh: 那是一个炎热的早晨，潮湿，典型的华盛顿夏季早晨。

sentences.en: There's probably 15 or 20 of us out there, mostly congressmen, a couple of senators.
sentences.zh: 当时大概有15到20人在场，主要是国会议员，还有几位参议员。

sentences.en: We get here about 6.15, 6.30.
sentences.zh: 我们大约6点15分、6点30分到达那里。

sentences.en: If you're familiar with the movie, remember the Titans?
sentences.zh: 如果你熟悉电影《光辉岁月》的话，还记得吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 记得。

sentences.en: We practice on their baseball field.
sentences.zh: 我们在他们的棒球场上练习。

sentences.en: They had come there to practice for the annual congressional charity baseball game, which is scheduled for today.
sentences.zh: 他们到那里是为了练习定于今天举行的年度国会慈善棒球赛。

sentences.en: But I was on deck about the hit batting practice on the third base side.
sentences.zh: 当时我正准备在三垒侧进行击球练习。

sentences.en: Some of the folks are in the outfield.
sentences.zh: 有些人正在外场。

sentences.en: Some of them are hanging around.
sentences.zh: 有些人正在附近闲逛。

sentences.en: The dugouts are at home plate, ready to, you know, practice their hitting.
sentences.zh: 休息区在本垒板处，准备进行击球练习。

sentences.en: And I hear a loud, bam!
sentences.zh: 然后我听到一声巨响，砰！

sentences.en: And shots ring out.
sentences.zh: 枪声响起。

sentences.en: The first shot was kind of an isolated shot.
sentences.zh: 第一声枪响是孤立的。

sentences.en: And everybody goes, kind of looks up and says, hey, what's that?
sentences.zh: 每个人都抬头看，心想，嘿，那是什么？

sentences.en: And I look around and behind third base in the third base dugout, which is cinder block, I see a rifle.
sentences.zh: 我环顾四周，在三垒后面的三垒休息区，那是煤渣砖砌的，我看到了一支步枪。

sentences.en: And then I hear another blam and I realize...
sentences.zh: 然后我又听到一声巨响，我意识到……

sentences.en: And then bedlam, people screaming, active shooter, folks sort of hitting the ground, duck and cover kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 接着是一片混乱，人们尖叫着，有活跃枪手，大家纷纷趴在地上，躲避掩护。

sentences.en: I run around to the first base side of home plate and we have a batting cage that's got plastic wrapped around it to stop foul balls and hide behind the plastic.
sentences.zh: 我跑到本垒板的一垒侧，那里有一个用塑料包裹的击球笼，用来挡住界外球，我就躲在塑料后面。

sentences.en: You know, that plastic's not real good.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那塑料其实不太管用。

sentences.en: But the shots kept coming.
sentences.zh: 但枪声不断。

sentences.en: Five, 10, 15 shots in a row.
sentences.zh: 连续五声、十声、十五声枪响。

sentences.en: The gun was a semi-automatic.
sentences.zh: 那是一把半自动武器。

sentences.en: It continues to fire at different people.
sentences.zh: 它继续向不同的人射击。

sentences.en: You can imagine all the people in the field scatter.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象场上所有人都四散奔逃。

sentences.en: At the same time, I hear Steve Scalise over near second base scream.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我听到二垒附近的史蒂夫·斯卡利斯在尖叫。

sentences.en: Steve Scalise, who was the majority whip, Republican congressman from Louisiana, was one of the folks out in the outfield.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·斯卡利斯是众议院多数党党鞭，来自路易斯安那州的共和党国会议员，是外场的人员之一。

sentences.en: He was out by second base in the middle of the field.
sentences.zh: 他当时在球场中间的二垒附近。

sentences.en: He gets struck by a bullet in the hip.
sentences.zh: 他的臀部中了一枪。

sentences.en: So he goes down but is moving and is crawling towards the outfield.
sentences.zh: 他倒下了，但还在移动，正向外场爬去。

sentences.en: The members of Congress who have sort of described this scene describe their anguish at seeing him go down but unable to get to him, right?
sentences.zh: 那些描述这一场景的国会议员们表达了他们看到他倒下却无法靠近他的痛苦，对吧？

sentences.en: They can't run out into the field when there's bullets flying all over the place.
sentences.zh: 当子弹到处乱飞时，他们无法冲进球场。

sentences.en: So they're hunkered down.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只能蜷缩着身子。

sentences.en: And I was blasting away.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在猛烈开火。

sentences.en: Fortunately, it was one of the good guys.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，那是好人之一。

sentences.en: And what happens, of course, is you've got two members of Mr. Scalise's Capitol Police detail, his protective detail,
sentences.zh: 当然，发生的事情是，斯卡利斯先生的国会警察安保小组有两名成员，他的保护小组，

sentences.en: who are at the game because he's a member of the Republican leadership, a senior person.
sentences.zh: 因为他是共和党领导层的一员，是一位资深人士，所以他们也在比赛现场。

sentences.en: They begin to return fire.
sentences.zh: 他们开始还击。

sentences.en: What we finally heard was the Capitol Hill police were turning gunfire.
sentences.zh: 我们最终听到的是国会山警察正在还击。

sentences.en: And these guys were real heroes.
sentences.zh: 这些人是真正的英雄。

sentences.en: And without them, I think everybody would have been killed.
sentences.zh: 如果没有他们，我想每个人都会被杀。

sentences.en: In addition, of course, people are calling 911 on their cell phones, screaming, we're under fire, we're under fire, there's a gunman.
sentences.zh: 此外，当然，人们用手机拨打911，尖叫着说，我们遭到袭击，我们遭到袭击，有枪手。

sentences.en: And so you also have the local police from Alexandria, Virginia,
sentences.zh: 所以你还有来自弗吉尼亚州亚历山大市的当地警察，

sentences.en: they also head to the scene and say they get there within about three minutes and they start engaging the suspect as well.
sentences.zh: 他们也赶往现场，并表示在大约三分钟内到达，他们也开始与嫌疑人交火。

sentences.en: Once we got the all clear that the shooter was down, we ran all into the outfield with leaving a trail of blood.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们得到枪手已被击倒的确认，我们就都跑进了外场，留下了一道血迹。

sentences.en: You know, I'm sad that he was shot, but he actually saved everybody's life by being there because he had the two security details.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我很遗憾他中枪了，但他当时在场实际上救了所有人的命，因为他有两名安保人员。

sentences.en: And I'm telling you, I don't know what happens if if no one's returning fire, because even with two professionals returning fire, one of them, I'm told,
sentences.zh: 我告诉你，我不知道如果没人还击会发生什么，因为即使有两名专业人员还击，据我所知，其中一人，

sentences.en: even being shot in the end was still protecting Scalise at the end.
sentences.zh: 即使最后中弹了，也还在保护斯卡利斯。

sentences.en: Mike, how many people were shot and what conditions are they in?
sentences.zh: 迈克，有多少人中枪？他们的情况如何？

sentences.en: So the latest we have is that there were a total of five people that were shot.
sentences.zh: 我们得到的最新消息是，总共有五人中枪。

sentences.en: That includes the shooter.
sentences.zh: 这包括枪手。

sentences.en: The shooter was killed.
sentences.zh: 枪手被击毙了。

sentences.en: The other four who were shot were people that the shooter shot with his weapons.
sentences.zh: 另外四名中枪者是枪手用武器射击的人。

sentences.en: And that includes Steve Scalise, one Capitol Police officer and congressional aide and this lobbyist who used to be a staff member for one of the members in Congress.
sentences.zh: 其中包括史蒂夫·斯卡利斯、一名国会警察、一名国会助手，以及这位曾经担任过国会议员幕僚的说客。

sentences.en: So Steve Scalise was listed most recently in critical condition.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·斯卡利斯最近被列为危急状态。

sentences.en: Having gone through surgery, the others were listed in serious condition or better.
sentences.zh: 在接受手术后，其他人被列为重伤或更好。

sentences.en: And Michael, who is this shooter?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，这个枪手是谁？

sentences.en: What do we know about him at this point?
sentences.zh: 目前我们对他了解多少？

sentences.en: So the shooter was a fellow by the name of James Hodgkinson.
sentences.zh: 枪手是一个名叫詹姆斯·霍奇金森的人。

sentences.en: Police tell us he's from a place called Belleville, Illinois, a suburb of St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 警方告诉我们他来自伊利诺伊州的贝尔维尔，是圣路易斯的一个郊区。

sentences.en: He was a home inspector, appears to have been residing in Alexandria, Virginia, here in the Washington area for more than a month.
sentences.zh: 他是一名房屋检查员，似乎已经在华盛顿地区的弗吉尼亚州亚历山大市居住了超过一个月。

sentences.en: And the most striking thing that we know about him, and we know this partly from interviews that we've conducted with his brother, a estranged brother, it looks like,
sentences.zh: 我们对他了解的最引人注目的事情，部分来自于我们对他兄弟——一个疏远的兄弟——的采访，看起来是这样，

sentences.en: and also from social media postings.
sentences.zh: 以及来自社交媒体的帖子。

sentences.en: He was a frequent user of Facebook and other social media.
sentences.zh: 他是Facebook和其他社交媒体的常客。

sentences.en: So what we know on Facebook, for example, is that he appears to have been a very passionate supporter of Bernie Sanders, was furulently anti-President Trump,
sentences.zh: 例如，我们在Facebook上了解到，他似乎是伯尼·桑德斯的忠实支持者，极其反对特朗普总统，

sentences.en: was part of groups that pledged to destroy Trump.
sentences.zh: 是誓言要摧毁特朗普的团体成员。

sentences.en: In one Facebook post, he said Trump had destroyed our democracy.
sentences.zh: 在一条Facebook帖子中，他说特朗普摧毁了我们的民主。

sentences.en: At one point, Mr. Hodgkinson signed an online petition calling for President Trump to be impeached.
sentences.zh: 有一次，霍奇金森先生签署了一份在线请愿书，呼吁弹劾特朗普总统。

sentences.en: And that was where he put the chilling comment, it's time to destroy Trump and co.
sentences.zh: 他在那里写下了令人不寒而栗的评论：是时候摧毁特朗普及其同伙了。

sentences.en: We also know from some interviews that one member of Congress believes that he encountered the gunman.
sentences.zh: 我们还从一些采访中得知，一位国会议员认为他遇到了枪手。

sentences.en: This member of Congress had been at the practice, had left early.
sentences.zh: 这位国会议员当时在练习现场，提前离开了。

sentences.en: As he went to the parking lot, he encountered a person who said, hey, who are those folks in there?
sentences.zh: 当他走到停车场时，他遇到了一个人，那人问：嘿，里面那些人是谁？

sentences.en: And he said, they're members of Congress playing baseball.
sentences.zh: 他说，他们是打棒球的国会议员。

sentences.en: And he said, well, are they Republicans or Democrats?
sentences.zh: 那人问，他们是共和党人还是民主党人？

sentences.en: And the congressman said, well, they're Republicans.
sentences.zh: 国会议员说，他们是共和党人。

sentences.en: So he asked which party?
sentences.zh: 所以他问是哪个党派？

sentences.en: He asked which party.
sentences.zh: 他问是哪个党派。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Mike, how are lawmakers from both parties reacting to what now seems, from your description, from all the reporting by the Times, to have been the targeting of one party?
sentences.zh: 迈克，两党的议员们对现在看来——根据你的描述，根据《时报》的所有报道——似乎是针对一个政党的袭击，有什么反应？

sentences.en: What are they saying?
sentences.zh: 他们说了什么？

sentences.en: So you saw Paul Ryan on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 你在国会山上看到了保罗·瑞安。

sentences.en: We are united.
sentences.zh: 我们团结一致。

sentences.en: We are united in our shock.
sentences.zh: 我们对震惊感到团结。

sentences.en: We are united in our anguish.
sentences.zh: 我们对痛苦感到团结。

sentences.en: An attack on one of us is an attack on all of us.
sentences.zh: 对我们其中一人的攻击就是对我们所有人的攻击。

sentences.en: Called on the entire Congress, Democrats and Republicans, to come together.
sentences.zh: 呼吁整个国会，民主党人和共和党人，团结起来。

sentences.en: To my colleagues, you're going to hear me say something you've never heard me say before.
sentences.zh: 对我的同事们，你们将听到我说一些你们从未听过的话。

sentences.en: I identify myself with the remarks of the speaker.
sentences.zh: 我认同议长的言论。

sentences.en: They're beautiful remarks, Mr. Speaker.
sentences.zh: 那是很棒的言论，议长先生。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for the sentiments that they represent.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢这些言论所代表的情感。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I'm really struck because we spend so much time watching these congressional hearings.
sentences.zh: 我真的很受触动，因为我们花了很多时间观看这些国会听证会。

sentences.en: It was just 48 hours ago that we had lawmakers who seem to be inhabiting an entirely different reality, angrily debating the big issues of the day, which are so divisive.
sentences.zh: 就在48小时前，我们还有议员似乎生活在完全不同的现实中，愤怒地辩论着当今那些极具分歧的重大议题。

sentences.en: The president, Russia, the election.
sentences.zh: 总统、俄罗斯、选举。

sentences.en: Are we at a point, Michael, where we only can come together in Washington after a tragedy like this?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我们是否到了只有在这样的悲剧之后才能在华盛顿团结起来的地步？

sentences.en: You know, I hope not.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我希望不是。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: I think one of the things that has been lost a little bit is that when you watch those hearings and you see the angry clashes and one lawmaker yelling at the other lawmaker or grilling somebody from the other party,
sentences.zh: 我认为有一点被忽略了，那就是当你观看那些听证会，看到愤怒的冲突，一位议员对另一位议员大喊大叫，或者盘问对方党派的人时，

sentences.en: I think that what the public that's watching that misses is what happens when the lights go off and the cameras go off.
sentences.zh: 我认为公众在观看时错过的是当灯光熄灭、摄像机关闭后发生的事情。

sentences.en: In many cases, even today, those members actually do like each other or at least have some respect for each other.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，即使在今天，这些议员实际上确实互相喜欢，或者至少互相尊重。

sentences.en: But that doesn't get translated on Twitter or on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有在Twitter或Facebook上传达出来。

sentences.en: Or to those who consume Twitter and Facebook, right.
sentences.zh: 或者对那些消费Twitter和Facebook的人来说，是这样。

sentences.en: Do you think that these lawmakers who say they're coming together now and who may break bread and play baseball together after all the yelling and screaming for the cameras,
sentences.zh: 你认为这些说现在要团结起来，并且在摄像机前大喊大叫后可能会一起吃饭、一起打棒球的议员们，

sentences.en: how do they square what just happened with their conduct when the cameras are on?
sentences.zh: 他们如何将刚刚发生的事情与他们在摄像机开启时的行为相协调？

sentences.en: You'd like to think that maybe the members of Congress might assign some responsibility to their actions and their comments and think that maybe at least when they're on the camera that there's some responsibility to think about how their words might be echoing across Twitter and Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你愿意认为也许国会议员可能会对他们的行为和评论承担一些责任，并认为也许至少当他们在摄像机前时，有责任考虑他们的话语如何在Twitter和Facebook上产生回响。

sentences.en: I'm a cynic here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里是个愤世嫉俗者。

sentences.en: I think that folks in that position are really good at excusing themselves and saying, look, that's not my responsibility or it's not my fault or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我认为处于那个位置的人非常擅长为自己开脱，说，看，那不是我的责任，或者那不是我的错，等等。

sentences.en: My guess is that after the shock of this moment wears off and we're back to regular order, so to speak, I think the policy differences are going to be just as raw.
sentences.zh: 我的猜测是，当这一时刻的震惊消退，我们回到所谓的正常秩序后，我认为政策分歧依然会非常尖锐。

sentences.en: And I think there's very little to suggest that the personal vitriol that is a regular part of our political discussion will change at all.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为几乎没有什么迹象表明作为我们政治讨论常规部分的个人刻薄言辞会有任何改变。

sentences.en: Michael, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: Happy to do it.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能这样做。

sentences.en: We may have our differences, but we do well in times like these to remember that everyone who serves in our nation's capital is here because, above all, they love our country.
sentences.zh: 我们可能有分歧，但在这样的时刻，我们最好记住，每一位在国家首都服务的人之所以在这里，是因为他们首先热爱我们的国家。

sentences.en: The annual congressional baseball game, which the lawmakers were practicing for when the shooting broke out, is still scheduled for today.
sentences.zh: 议员们在枪击事件爆发时正在练习的年度国会棒球赛仍定于今天举行。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个关于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this, like,
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在黑胶唱片时代在夜总会当DJ的时候，每天晚上你都要带着你最珍视的300件物品去工作，你把DJ台变成了一个，就像，

sentences.zh: 充满活力的、展示精美50年历史文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 一个月的时间让你越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅用户每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Two hours after the shooting in Virginia, Donald Trump Jr., the president's son, retweeted this.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州枪击事件发生两小时后，总统的儿子小唐纳德·特朗普转发了这条推文。

sentences.en: Events like today are exactly why we took issue with the New York elite glorifying the assassination of our president.
sentences.zh: 像今天这样的事件正是我们反对纽约精英美化暗杀我们总统的原因。

sentences.en: That was a reference to a new production of Julius Caesar, one in which the slain Roman dictator looks a lot like President Trump.
sentences.zh: 这是指一部新的《朱利叶斯·凯撒》剧作，其中被杀的罗马独裁者看起来很像特朗普总统。

sentences.en: Michael Cooper, what happens in Act 3, Scene 1 of Julius Caesar?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·库珀，《朱利叶斯·凯撒》第三幕第一场发生了什么？

sentences.en: Julius Caesar, the great war hero, is in his element.
sentences.zh: 伟大的战争英雄尤利乌斯·凯撒正处于他的人生巅峰。

sentences.en: He's in Rome going to the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 他正在前往罗马国会大厦的路上。

sentences.en: He's wearing his white toga and probably his laurel wreath.
sentences.zh: 他穿着白色的托加长袍，可能还戴着月桂花环。

sentences.en: He's the man in charge and he's on the cusp of taking control of all of Rome.
sentences.zh: 他是掌权者，正处于掌控整个罗马的关键时刻。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, you have the senators who are afraid that their Republican way of government is about to disappear,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，参议员们担心他们共和制的政府即将消失，

sentences.en: that he's going to seize all the power and that suddenly the senators will be completely powerless.
sentences.zh: 担心他会攫取所有权力，而参议员们将瞬间变得毫无实权。

sentences.en: And so they hatch a conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们策划了一场阴谋。

sentences.en: Oh, Caesar!
sentences.zh: 噢，凯撒！

sentences.en: Hence wilt thou lift up a limber?
sentences.zh: 难道你要举起这柔弱的肢体吗？

sentences.en: Great Caesar!
sentences.zh: 伟大的凯撒！

sentences.en: Doth no brutus bootless kneel!
sentences.zh: 难道没有布鲁图斯在徒劳地跪求吗！

sentences.en: And suddenly, you know, right on the steps of the Capitol, one after another, they stab him to death.
sentences.zh: 突然间，就在国会大厦的台阶上，他们一个接一个地将他刺死。

sentences.en: And the final blow is delivered by Brutus.
sentences.zh: 最后一击是由布鲁图斯完成的。

sentences.en: Et tu.
sentences.zh: 还有你吗？

sentences.en: Et tu, Brute, then fall, Caesar.
sentences.zh: 还有你吗，布鲁图？那么，倒下吧，凯撒。

sentences.en: Even you.
sentences.zh: 连你也是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Would do this to me.
sentences.zh: 竟然会这样对我。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And suddenly, the play changes direction completely, 180 degrees.
sentences.zh: 突然间，这部剧的方向完全改变了，来了个180度大转弯。

sentences.en: And these conspirators who thought they were saving the Republic by killing the despot, in fact, set in motion a series of events that kills the Republic.
sentences.zh: 这些以为通过杀死暴君就能拯救共和国的阴谋家们，实际上引发了一系列导致共和国灭亡的事件。

sentences.en: A bloody civil war breaks out, factions arise, and, you know, even worse, tyranny lies ahead.
sentences.zh: 血腥的内战爆发了，派系林立，甚至更糟的是，暴政即将来临。

sentences.en: Michael, is there a line in Julius Caesar that stands out to you, even now?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，在《尤利乌斯·凯撒》中，有没有哪句台词即使在今天也让你印象深刻？

sentences.en: Well, given this week, you can't help but think of the moment when one of the conspirators turns to Brutus and says,
sentences.zh: 嗯，考虑到本周发生的事，你不得不想到那个时刻，其中一名阴谋家转向布鲁图斯说：

sentences.en: How many ages hence shall this, our lofty scene, be acted over in states unborn and accents yet unknown?
sentences.zh: “多少个时代以后，我们这出崇高的戏，将在未出生的国家和未知的口音中重演？”

sentences.en: What do you make of that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有何看法？

sentences.en: It's a brilliant moment because on the one hand, Shakespeare is talking about the fact that
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝妙的时刻，因为一方面，莎士比亚在谈论这样一个事实：

sentences.en: he's showing something to London audiences 1,600 odd years after the event that it happened.
sentences.zh: 他在事件发生一千六百多年后，向伦敦的观众展示这一幕。

sentences.en: So he's talking about himself.
sentences.zh: 所以他是在谈论他自己。

sentences.en: But I think he's also perhaps imagining a future for his own play.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他可能也在构想他这部剧的未来。

sentences.en: This has since traveled the whole world and been done in any number of accents and with any number of interpretations.
sentences.zh: 此后，这部剧传遍了全世界，以各种口音和各种解读方式被演绎。

sentences.en: All Rome was wild with joy.
sentences.zh: 整个罗马都陷入了狂喜之中。

sentences.en: Julius Caesar, having conquered his great rival, Pompeo...
sentences.zh: 尤利乌斯·凯撒在征服了他的劲敌庞培之后……

sentences.en: My countrymen!
sentences.zh: 我的同胞们！

sentences.en: Good countrymen, let me depart alone and for my sake stay here with Antony.
sentences.zh: 善良的同胞们，让我独自离开，为了我的缘故，请留在这里陪安东尼。

sentences.en: Hail Caesar!
sentences.zh: 凯撒万岁！

sentences.en: Hail!
sentences.zh: 万岁！

sentences.en: Only one survivor, sir!
sentences.zh: 只有一个幸存者，长官！

sentences.en: Ah!
sentences.zh: 啊！

sentences.en: Throw him to the floor!
sentences.zh: 把他扔到地板上！

sentences.en: What, sir?
sentences.zh: 什么，长官？

sentences.en: Throw him to the floor!
sentences.zh: 把他扔到地板上！

sentences.en: Ah!
sentences.zh: 啊！

sentences.en: Why can this story be interpreted to fit so many different political moments?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个故事可以被解读以适应如此多不同的政治时刻？

sentences.en: What is it about this play that makes it so malleable?
sentences.zh: 这部剧有什么特质使它如此具有可塑性？

sentences.en: Well, one of the brilliant things about this play is that Shakespeare doesn't tell you what to think exactly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这部剧最精彩的地方之一就是莎士比亚并没有明确告诉你该怎么想。

sentences.en: You know, it's never quite clear to what extent is he sympathizing with the conspirators or condemning them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他到底在多大程度上同情阴谋家，或者在多大程度上谴责他们，从来都不太清楚。

sentences.en: To what extent is he condemning Julius Caesar or sympathizing with him?
sentences.zh: 他在多大程度上谴责尤利乌斯·凯撒，或者同情他？

sentences.en: He puts enough on both sides of every matter that it's really fertile ground if you're a director who wants to impose a new look at it.
sentences.zh: 他在每一件事的两面都投入了足够多的内容，如果你是一位想要赋予它新视角导演，这确实是一片肥沃的土壤。

sentences.en: And directors have done this brilliantly for almost a century now.
sentences.zh: 近一个世纪以来，导演们一直出色地做到了这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, ever since 1937, you had Orson Welles and his legendary Mercury Theater in New York City on the eve of World War II.
sentences.zh: 我是说，自1937年以来，奥逊·威尔斯和他在纽约市传奇的水星剧团在二战前夕就做过尝试。

sentences.en: Suddenly, they made Julius Caesar a Mussolini-like character, and the play became about the creeping tyranny of fascism.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他们把尤利乌斯·凯撒塑造成了一个类似墨索里尼的角色，这部剧变成了关于法西斯主义悄然蔓延的暴政。

sentences.en: There was even one at Trinity Rep about two years ago where Caesar was played by a woman who wore a white pantsuit, which reminded people, of course, of Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 大约两年前，三位一体剧团甚至上演过一个版本，凯撒由一名穿着白色裤装的女性扮演，这当然让人想起了希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: So tell us about the Donald Trump interpretation.
sentences.zh: 那么，给我们讲讲唐纳德·特朗普的解读版本吧。

sentences.en: It's currently being put on by the public theater in New York.
sentences.zh: 它目前正在纽约的公共剧院上演。

sentences.en: Well, Oskar Eustace, who's the artistic director of the public theater, had in mind making Julius Caesar into a Trump-like figure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，公共剧院的艺术总监奥斯卡·尤斯塔斯，有意将尤利乌斯·凯撒塑造成一个类似特朗普的人物。

sentences.en: And so suddenly he has a shock of blonde hair.
sentences.zh: 于是他突然有了一头金色的乱发。

sentences.en: He has an overlong red necktie.
sentences.zh: 他系着一条过长的红领带。

sentences.en: He has a wife who has a recognizably Slovenian accent.
sentences.zh: 他有一位有着明显斯洛文尼亚口音的妻子。

sentences.en: He has a gold bathtub.
sentences.zh: 他有一个金浴缸。

sentences.en: It becomes a very Trumpian Caesar.
sentences.zh: 这变成了一个非常“特朗普式”的凯撒。

sentences.en: What did you see that surprised you and appalled you?
sentences.zh: 你看到了什么让你感到惊讶和震惊？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I was expecting it to be a classic rendition of Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，我原本以为这会是《尤利乌斯·凯撒》的经典演绎。

sentences.en: I think the idea was to look at this moment when all these norms of politics are being upended and situate the play in that world.
sentences.zh: 我想其构思是审视当下这个政治准则被颠覆的时刻，并将该剧置于那个世界中。

sentences.en: I mean, they didn't specifically say it, but his hair, blonde, reddish, had those ties tied too long.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们没有明确说出来，但他的头发，金中带红，领带系得太长了。

sentences.en: No audience member could see this and possibly fail to mistake who's being assassinated and what's going on.
sentences.zh: 没有观众看到这一幕会认不出谁正在被暗杀，以及发生了什么。

sentences.en: So I'm like, oh, I want to watch this central scene of the play, Act 3, Scene 1.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，哦，我想看看这部剧的核心场景，第三幕第一场。

sentences.en: So the Trump-like character is yanked from a podium and three or four men and a woman are, they're tearing off his jacket.
sentences.zh: 那个类似特朗普的角色被从讲台上拽了下来，三四个男人和一个女人正在撕扯他的外套。

sentences.en: They're stabbing him from the front, from behind.
sentences.zh: 他们从正面、背面刺向他。

sentences.en: He's trying to kick them off.
sentences.zh: 他试图把他们踢开。

sentences.en: The scene evokes the assassination of our current president and therefore it's, it's hard to watch.
sentences.zh: 这一幕让人联想到我们现任总统的遇刺，因此，这很难看下去。

sentences.en: It's shocking and I think it's meant to be shocking.
sentences.zh: 这令人震惊，而且我认为它本意就是为了让人震惊。

sentences.en: It's horrifying and I think is meant to be horrifying.
sentences.zh: 这令人毛骨悚然，而且我认为它本意就是为了让人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: It's, it's, it's supposed to be upsetting.
sentences.zh: 它，它，它本该让人感到不安。

sentences.en: It's supposed to be really upsetting is what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 你是说它本该让人感到非常不安。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That, that's the point.
sentences.zh: 那，那就是重点。

sentences.en: You, you can't do it and not make it upsetting.
sentences.zh: 你，你不可能在不让人感到不安的情况下完成它。

sentences.en: That would be to misjudge the whole play.
sentences.zh: 那将是对整部剧的误读。

sentences.en: Hamlet said the purpose of playing from the first till today was and is to hold up as to her a mirror to nature.
sentences.zh: 哈姆雷特曾说，演戏的宗旨，从古至今，就是像照镜子一样反映自然。

sentences.en: To show the age of his form and pressure.
sentences.zh: 展示时代的形态和压力。

sentences.en: Actually quoted that line from Cassius about the accents yet unknown in his program note.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他在节目单中引用了卡西乌斯关于“未知的口音”的那句台词。

sentences.en: Because I think they anticipated that there would be some controversy here.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为他们预料到这里会引起一些争议。

sentences.en: And his gloss on the play is that Julius Caesar is a warning parable to those who try to fight for democracy by undemocratic means.
sentences.zh: 他对这部剧的诠释是，《尤利乌斯·凯撒》是对那些试图通过非民主手段争取民主的人的警示寓言。

sentences.en: And he writes that to fight the tyrant does not mean imitating him.
sentences.zh: 他写道，对抗暴君并不意味着模仿他。

sentences.en: And that's the thing about Julius Caesar is, although there's been an incredible uproar about the idea of having a staged assassination of the president in Central Park.
sentences.zh: 这就是《尤利乌斯·凯撒》的关键所在，尽管关于在中央公园上演总统遇刺的构想引起了巨大的轩然大波。

sentences.en: Look, Julius Caesar is not the anarchist cookbook.
sentences.zh: 听着，《尤利乌斯·凯撒》不是《无政府主义者食谱》。

sentences.en: It's not a pro-assassination play.
sentences.zh: 它不是一部支持暗杀的剧。

sentences.en: If anything, it's showing the horrors that are unleashed when, even if you think you have righteousness on your side, when you take matters into your own hands and do it, chaos,
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么的话，它展示了当你自认为站在正义一边，却擅自行动时所释放出的恐怖，随之而来的是混乱、

sentences.en: bloodshed, insanity follows.
sentences.zh: 流血和疯狂。

sentences.en: And I think that's the message of all Julius Caesars and the one that's being played in Central Park right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是所有《尤利乌斯·凯撒》版本以及目前在中央公园上演的这一版所传达的信息。

sentences.en: That neither Shakespeare nor the public theater could possibly advocate violence as a solution to political problems and certainly not assassination.
sentences.zh: 无论是莎士比亚还是公共剧院，都不可能主张用暴力作为解决政治问题的方案，更不用说暗杀了。

sentences.en: Now, that being said, the play has clearly inspired violence in the past and it's inspired assassins in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，这部剧过去显然曾激发过暴力，也曾激发过刺客。

sentences.en: You know, John Wilkes Booth, not very long before he killed Lincoln, was in a production of Julius Caesar in New York City and he was clearly moved by it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，约翰·威尔克斯·布斯在刺杀林肯前不久，曾在纽约市参与过《尤利乌斯·凯撒》的演出，他显然深受触动。

sentences.en: After he had killed Lincoln, when he was on the run, he wrote in his diaries, he complained that he was being hunted for doing what Brutus was celebrated for.
sentences.zh: 在他刺杀林肯后，在逃亡期间，他在日记中写道，他抱怨自己因为做了布鲁图斯被歌颂的事情而遭到追捕。

sentences.en: Similarly, there was, you know, Klaus von Stauffenberg who was in one of the failed plots to assassinate Hitler and in various accounts of that plot, the Operation Valkyrie,
sentences.zh: 同样，你知道，克劳斯·冯·施陶芬贝格曾参与过刺杀希特勒的失败阴谋之一，在关于那次阴谋（瓦尔基里行动）的各种记录中，

sentences.en: they say that he had a copy of Julius Caesar on his desk with bits annotated there.
sentences.zh: 他们说他的桌上放着一本《尤利乌斯·凯撒》，上面还有标注。

sentences.en: So, while most people would read the play as anti-assassination, it still has inspired people who think on some level, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然大多数人会将这部剧解读为反暗杀，但它仍然激发了那些在某种程度上认为，你知道，

sentences.en: that it shows people trying to take arms against a tyrant.
sentences.zh: 它展示了人们试图拿起武器对抗暴君的人。

sentences.en: Do you think that maybe this version is hitting a nerve in a way the other versions didn't because it's too literal of a portrayal?
sentences.zh: 你认为这个版本是否因为表现得太直白，而触动了其他版本没有触动的神经？

sentences.en: It's too close to President Trump.
sentences.zh: 它太接近特朗普总统了。

sentences.en: Well, it got too close for Delta Airlines, which decided it no longer wanted to be the official airlines of the public theater and pulled its sponsorship.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它对达美航空来说太接近了，他们决定不再担任公共剧院的官方航空公司，并撤回了赞助。

sentences.en: It got too close for Bank of America, which pulled their support from this production, but said that they would continue to support the theater's other work.
sentences.zh: 它对美国银行来说也太接近了，他们撤回了对这部剧的支持，但表示将继续支持该剧院的其他作品。

sentences.en: Just when you thought it was impossible, liberal left-wing nutjobs in Hollywood and Broadway have reached a new low.
sentences.zh: 就在你以为不可能的时候，好莱坞和百老汇的自由派左翼疯子们又达到了一个新的低点。

sentences.en: It's become a rallying cry of the right.
sentences.zh: 这已经成为了右翼的集结口号。

sentences.en: What was the reaction from the crowd?
sentences.zh: 观众的反应如何？

sentences.en: The liberal New York crowd.
sentences.zh: 那些自由派的纽约观众。

sentences.en: I think they accepted it and were fine with it.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们接受了它，并且觉得没问题。

sentences.en: It was funny.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: It was entertainment.
sentences.zh: 这是一种娱乐。

sentences.en: But to me, he's the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，他是美国总统。

sentences.en: It's gone too far for the president's family, but it didn't go too far for everybody.
sentences.zh: 这对总统的家人来说太过分了，但对所有人来说并非如此。

sentences.en: I think the public theater has seen an outpouring of donations from individuals who support their attempts to do, you know, do uncomfortable work.
sentences.zh: 我认为公共剧院看到了来自个人的大量捐款，他们支持剧院尝试去，你知道，去完成那些令人不适的作品。

sentences.en: And, you know, the New York Times continues to be a sponsor of the public theater.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，《纽约时报》继续担任公共剧院的赞助商。

sentences.en: This is a production that's transcended eras, as we've established, I mean, hundreds of years of time.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所确定的，这是一部跨越了时代的制作，我是说，跨越了数百年的时间。

sentences.en: And it's transcended governments and countries.
sentences.zh: 它跨越了政府和国家。

sentences.en: Do you think there's something about our current political context that's making this even more upsetting than it has been in the past?
sentences.zh: 你认为我们当前的政治背景是否让它比过去更令人不安？

sentences.en: Or have these previous depictions been just as upsetting for the audiences in their time?
sentences.zh: 还是说，之前的这些描绘在当时对观众来说也同样令人不安？

sentences.en: Well, I think this is a moment when Americans of all political stripes are sort of on a knife edge, where long-time norms are being broken,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是一个所有政治倾向的美国人都处于刀尖上的时刻，长期的准则正在被打破，

sentences.en: politics doesn't work the way you thought it did, things that you thought you might never see you're seeing.
sentences.zh: 政治运作方式不再是你所想的那样，你以为永远不会看到的事情正在发生。

sentences.en: And so I think there is a heightened awareness and heightened sensitivity and a kind of a combustibility to American life right now that makes it both a very appropriate time to watch Julius Caesar and to think about it and reflect on it and look at how these issues have played out throughout history,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，美国生活现在有一种高度的觉知、高度的敏感和一种易燃性，这使得现在既是观看《尤利乌斯·凯撒》、思考它、反思它并审视这些问题在历史上是如何演变的非常合适的时机，

sentences.en: but also can lead to strong hyper-partisan reactions to it as well.
sentences.zh: 但也可能导致对它强烈的党派化反应。

sentences.en: I think it's a time that people feel like anything could happen on some level.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个人们在某种程度上觉得什么都可能发生的时代。

sentences.en: And I think that's why it's interesting to see something, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么看到一些东西很有趣，你知道，

sentences.en: a 400-year-old play about a 2,000-year-old piece of history can be elucidating and maybe even a little comforting.
sentences.zh: 一部关于两千年前历史的四百年老剧，可以起到启发作用，甚至可能带来一点安慰。

sentences.en: Art has something to say about the great civic issues of our time and to say that like drama, democracy depends.
sentences.zh: 艺术对我们这个时代的重大公民议题有话要说，并说像戏剧一样，民主取决于。

sentences.en: On the conflict of different points of view.
sentences.zh: 不同观点的冲突。

sentences.en: Nobody owns the truth.
sentences.zh: 没有人拥有真理。

sentences.en: We all own the culture.
sentences.zh: 我们都拥有文化。

sentences.en: Welcome to the public.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到公共剧院。

sentences.en: Welcome to Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《尤利乌斯·凯撒》。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: The Times is reporting on new information that suggests the special counsel investigating Russia's meddling in the election is preparing to investigate whether President Trump obstructed justice.
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道了新的信息，表明调查俄罗斯干预选举的特别检察官正准备调查特朗普总统是否妨碍了司法公正。

sentences.en: Special counsel Robert Mueller has reportedly requested interviews with three high-ranking current and former intelligence officials amid questions about whether President Trump requested their help in trying to end the FBI's investigation into Michael Flynn.
sentences.zh: 据报道，特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒已要求采访三位现任和前任高级情报官员，以调查特朗普总统是否曾要求他们帮助结束联邦调查局对迈克尔·弗林的调查。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: Daily listeners often ask how you can support this show.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》的听众经常问如何支持这个节目。

sentences.en: The answer is through a subscription to The Times.
sentences.zh: 答案是通过订阅《时报》。

sentences.en: It's the journalistic engine that makes this show.
sentences.zh: 它是支撑这个节目的新闻引擎。

sentences.en: The Times is now offering Daily listeners a free trial week of digital access.
sentences.zh: 《时报》现在为《每日新闻》的听众提供为期一周的免费数字访问试用。

sentences.en: Visit nytimes.com slash daily trial to sign up.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com 斜杠 daily trial 进行注册。

sentences.en: That's nytimes.com slash daily trial.
sentences.zh: 即 nytimes.com 斜杠 daily trial。

sentences.en: And thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周在《Wirecutter》节目中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑睡眠环境的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是一件非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《The Wirecutter Show》。
